newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes steady in active trade.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes steady in active trade.

text.p: The North Sea physical market was active on Wednedsay with Dated Brent holding steady at parity to November paper and gas oil grades fetching a higher premium amid strong refiner buying traders said.

November paper was notionally assessed lower at around $23.10/15 a barrel late in the day but there were no trades. The prompt intermonth spread was not discussed late in the day with no bids or offers seen.
Nov/Dec was firmer at +50/+53 cents and Dec/Jan virtually unchanged at +58/+60.
Next week's CFDs weakened to -6/-4 cents in thin trade.
Wet dealers saw Dated Brent holding current levels after three cargoes were sold at November evens with no overhang.
"Brent is certainly moving and is not being stacked up," a wet trader said.
"I don't see Dated collapse from here any more. If you go to the end of the month, it will be November minus because of the backwardation," another oil company trader said.

A trader believed putting together a VLCC for South Africa bought two Oct 13-15 Brent cargoes on Wednesday but there were some doubts about the feasibility of the dates due to the late availability of the tanker.
One wet dealer said this could result in some of the Brent cargoes held by the trader reappearing on the market.
Another Brent cargo loading Oct 16-18 was sold to a refiner at November flat. The two Brent dates which turned wet on Wednesday were kept by an equity producer and a trader.

"I do believe that Brent is finding a little bit of support here because it is cheap compared with the other grades and I'm surprised that people are paying up to 40 over Dated for Oseberg but I guess so long as gas oil is firm people will buy it," he added.
